endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Note which AI systems have been validated using which tools, and which have not yet been validated.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: This validation should be performed by the developer and implementer teams; documentation that the AI solution performs as expected should be collected.

commentary.bottom_line: No study has tested whether recording local validation status and flagging unvalidated high-risk AI systems reduces the number of such systems left in clinical use, and no study supplied here measures how often that hazard occurs. The recommendation rests on two CHAI framework documents, one rated must and one rated should.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies that test the practice and zero studies that document the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The support consists of expert framework guidance, which reflects consensus rather than measured effect.

No study supplied here reports how many unvalidated high-risk systems remain in use or what harm follows from them. Without such data, the size of the safety gain from a validation registry and a remediation flag cannot be estimated.

The CHAI governance playbook states the practice as a must and asks committees to note which systems have and have not been validated. The CHAI Assurance Standards Guide rates it should and assigns validation to developer and implementer teams. Both sources are voluntary frameworks and do not carry regulatory force.

commentary.research_gap: Studies should first measure how many AI systems in use at health systems lack local validation and how many of those are high risk. Studies should then compare the share of unvalidated high-risk systems that are remediated or withdrawn, and the time that takes, in systems that keep a validation registry with priority flags against systems that do not.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems cannot tell from this evidence whether validation records capture performance in these groups, and a system marked as validated may not have been checked in the patients it serves.
